title: Cross-model config delta detector for typed JSON outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: implement an automated detector that ties evals and runtime telemetry to configuration/model changes and flags quality regressions for typed JSON outputs.

Background: We have recurring incidents where subtle changes to runtime config (quantization, kernel selection, batching policy) or model variants cause structured-output failures (missing keys, type mismatches, shifted arrays). Existing evaluation runs validate a static snapshot of schema conformance but are not automatically correlated with config deltas or rollout events. That delay increases MTTR and requires manual triage.

Scope: prototype a "delta-eval" pipeline that: (1) detects a config or model change event from the deployment control plane; (2) runs a targeted eval suite anchored to a small stable prompt corpus; (3) computes both strict JSON Schema validation and a soft-structure score that captures semantic/ordering deviations; (4) surfaces a ranked list of affected prompts and the likely delta attribution (config change X vs model version Y); (5) creates an automatic incident ticket or alert when thresholds are exceeded.

User stories:
- As an SRE on-call, when a rollout changes quantization profile I want the system to triage schema regressions and show the top 10 failing samples so I can decide rollback vs mitigate.
- As an ML engineer, when we promote a new model build I want a pre-rollout delta-eval summary showing likely schema-risk so I can adjust temperature/prompt or pin a fallback.

Non-goals: full test-suite regression at scale (we're targeting a small anchored corpus for speed), schema auto-repair, and replacing human triage for complex logical failures.

Metrics to drive: schema-failure-rate delta (absolute and %), soft-structure-score drop, median time from change to alert, false positive rate of detector.

Implementation highlights: automated trigger from deployment events, a lightweight evaluation runner (k=200 anchored prompts by default), two parallel validators (jsonschema strict pass/fail and a soft-schema comparator based on normalized AST similarity and token alignment), per-sample attribution tags, and an alerting threshold with noisy-gain suppression to avoid churn.
acceptance_criteria: Detector watches model/version and runtime-config change events in the control plane and starts a delta-eval job within 2 minutes of the event
Delta-eval runs on the anchored prompt corpus (configurable, default 200 prompts) and returns results within 8 minutes for typical change profiles
System computes strict JSON Schema pass rate and a soft-structure score for each sample and aggregates a delta compared to the baseline snapshot
Alert rule triggers when strict pass rate drops by >=5 percentage points AND soft-structure score median drops by >=0.08, creating an automatic ticket and Slack notification to #oncall-inference
Results page links to top 20 failing samples, diffs between outputs (baseline vs new), and a suggested likely cause (config parameter mostly correlated with failures)
On-call playbook documented and linked on the detector results page with rollback and mitigation steps
updates: 2026-02-18: Spec drafted during weekly Reliability sync. Decided to target anchored corpus approach for speed and deterministic triage. (Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Typed+Output+Delta+Eval+Spec)

2026-02-24: Prototype runner implemented (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/247) that executes evaluation jobs on dedicated test pool and stores output artifacts in s3://redwood-evals/delta-run/ENG-19824/

2026-03-02: Early results from quantization change test showed a 7.4% strict schema pass-rate drop on 200-sample corpus. Soft-structure score decreased 0.12. Captured sample diffs and added initial attribution heuristics based on config delta correlation.
2026-03-05: Demo to PM and SRE; feedback: include per-field type histograms and make alert thresholds configurable per-customer. Added to backlog as follow-up (ENG-19910).

2026-03-08: Code review feedback addressed: added faster jsonschema streaming validator, reduced memory footprint, added telemetry events for 'delta_eval.started' and 'delta_eval.completed'. PR merged to feature branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/256

2026-03-10: Integration test failing intermittently under heavy concurrent rollout events; root cause appears to be contention in the eval job queue. Added short-term mitigation by rate-limiting delta-eval starts and long-term follow-up ENG-20045 to refactor queue service.
decision_log: Use anchored small corpus vs full eval to keep time-to-alert low (trade-off: lower coverage but faster triage)
Dual validation: strict jsonschema + soft-structure score to reduce false positives on semantically-equivalent formatting changes
Alert thresholds chosen conservatively for P1 path; make per-project tuning available in console
Initial attribution heuristic uses Spearman correlation between config change delta and per-sample failure indicator; will iterate to more principled causal tests later
playbook: 1) When alert fires, open auto-created ticket and notify #oncall-inference with link to delta-eval results
2) Review top 5 failing samples and compare baseline vs new outputs; check per-field type histograms
3) If failures map to a specific config (e.g., int8 quantization), rollback that change or pin model variant and escalate to ML eng
4) If failures are model-specific, rollback model rollout and kick off full evaluation run and regression investigation
5) Update the detector baseline after an approved rollout to avoid repeated alerts for intentional changes
